To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the commodity price shocks affect the Mexican economy through the cost of living and the profitability of the agricultural sector; (ii) the welfare effects of the shocks depend on the income distribution; (iii) indexing wages to prices hurts the poorest households; and (iv) the commodity price increases in the 1970s and 1980s were welfare reducing for the poorest rural families.
the international commodity price shock has a negative effect on the general index of cost of living, but a positive effect on the profitability of major crops and, consequently, on rural welfare.
the international commodity price shock has a positive effect on the profitability of the agricultural sector, a negative effect on the cost of living and a positive effect on rural welfare.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the short-run effects of commodity prices on Mexican economy.
the short run effects on the cost of living of the international shocks in the prices of the major crops in Mexico.
the analysis of the short run effects on the cost of living, the income distribution and the welfare of the households of the international commodity prices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the international commodity price shock is not a major problem for Mexican households.
the commodity price shocks in the international markets have a small but negative welfare effect on the poorest rural families in Mexico.
the commodity price shocks in the short run have a negative impact in the cost of living, and a positive impact in the rural income.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international price shocks are not as negative for the rural sector as it is usually thought.
, in the short run, the international commodity price shock has a small impact on the general index of prices in Mexico.
the price effects of commodity price shocks are not as large as usually thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the international price shocks have a limited short term impact on the Mexican economy.
the international commodity price shock is not a major threat for Mexico’s economic development.
the short-run effects of international commodity price shocks are not necessarily negative, especially for the poorest rural families.
